newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical firms say their sick pay different.
newsitem.headline: German chemical firms say their sick pay different.

text.p: The German chemical sector employers federation said on Wednesday that contracts in its industry were different to those in other sectors in that they clearly permitted sick pay cuts in line with a new law.

Speaking after the collapse of talks about sick pay cuts in the engineering industry, the BAVC employers group said the wage contracts of chemical workers meant sick payments were "expressly linked" to the overall law on the matter.

That was changed last month to allow sick payments be made at 80 percent of full salary instead of the current 100 percent. Unions in some sectors have said however that the law should not override clauses in existing wage contracts.
The IG Chemie trade union has also demanded talks on the planned cuts. Some 13,000 workers at BASF AG walked off the job earlier this month in protest.
The BAVC said the talks with IG Chemie would go ahead this Friday.
